questions.q: How large an emergency fund does Clements recommend?
a: Three to six months of living expenses
One to two weeks of take-home pay
A full year of your current salary
Ten percent of your total net worth
questions.why: The first lesson says to save this much and keep it somewhere that is hard to reach.

questions.q: Why do we overspend and plan poorly, according to the summary?
a: Instincts inherited from ancestors who seized whatever they found
Advertising has become far more persuasive than before
Banks make credit much too easy to obtain
Schools never teach students how to budget
questions.why: The second lesson says our hunter-gatherer minds push us to overindulge and think short-term.

questions.q: What limit does the summary put on fixed monthly expenses?
a: No more than 50% of pre-tax income
No more than 30% of pre-tax income
No more than 70% of pre-tax income
No more than 90% of pre-tax income
questions.why: The second lesson says keeping fixed costs under half of pre-tax pay leaves room for taxes, savings and fun.

questions.q: How does the summary define frugality?
a: Living below your means and below what you could spend
Never buying anything you genuinely enjoy
Tracking every purchase in a budgeting app
Earning more through a second job
questions.why: The third lesson describes it as a habit of buying only what you need, not a life without pleasure.

questions.q: Which costly habits does the summary say also damage your health?
a: Smoking, drinking and gambling
Eating out and traveling
Streaming and gaming
Buying coffee and clothes
questions.why: The third lesson says these habits drain both money and vitality, so quitting pays twice.
